script.cite: Books V-VI printed pp.30-31 = book5-6.pdf PDF pp.36-37 (procedure p.31); rule: rotary at 0, power on, transmission starts only at pushbutton 6; derived from topology: every + source (6H, 6Y, 5H, 4H, 5Y) sits on an open N.O. contact or pushbutton arm, so no coil or lamp has a path
script.quote: Set the rotary switch at 0 and turn power on.

script.cite: Books V-VI printed pp.30-31 = book5-6.pdf PDF pp.36-37 (procedure p.31, rule p.30); rule: first revolution transmits "JO"; derived from topology: 6Y(+)-6X puts + on 6F/D17/D16, relay 6 pulls in and latches 6H-6G-6F; the wiper on D0 feeds 5L-5N(relay 5 N.C.)-4F, relay 4 latches 4H-4G-4F and relay 3 (3F/4G) follows it; relay 5 is fed only from D15
script.quote: That is, on its first revolution the rotary switch will instruct the computer to transmit "JO"; on its second revolution it will instruct the computer to transmit "HN."

script.quote: That is, on its first revolution the rotary switch will instruct the computer to transmit "JO"; on its second revolution it will instruct the computer to transmit "HN."

script.quote: That is, on its first revolution the rotary switch will instruct the computer to transmit "JO"; on its second revolution it will instruct the computer to transmit "HN."

script.cite: Books V-VI printed pp.30-31 = book5-6.pdf PDF pp.36-37 (procedure p.31); rule: the transmission alternates JO and HN; derived from topology: at D15 relay 4 out feeds 4N-5E, shorting relay 5 coil (5F + by latch), relay 5 drops; at D0 relay 5 out feeds 5L-5N-4F, relays 4 and 3 pull in and 4 latches; revolution 3 repeats revolution 1
script.quote: Notice that as the rotary switch turns the computer alternately transmits "JO" and "HN."

note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect and until is derived by hand from the 38-wire topology and the p.30 rule (first revolution JO, second HN), not printed; the printed fixture C2/V-EXP17 covers the lamps flashing and the pushbutton 5 stop. No erratum changes a wire (ER-37 is prose), so the wires are as printed. Topology: relay 6 latches 6H(+)-6G-6F and 6G/D17 runs the motor (D18/M-), D16/D17 puts + on the wiper; relays 4 and 5 form a toggle stepped by D0 and D15: D0 feeds 5L, setting relay 4 (5N-4F) when relay 5 is out and shorting relay 4 (5K-4E) when it is in; D15 feeds 4L, setting relay 5 (4K-5F) when relay 4 is in and shorting relay 5 (4N-5E) when it is out; relay 3 (3F/4G) follows relay 4 and selects the path. Lamp map: D2 light 6 always; D3, D4, D5, D12 via 3H, light 5 with relay 3 in, light 6 with it out; D11 light 5 always; D13 via 3L-3K light 5 with relay 3 in, nothing with it out. Script choices, not printed: pushbutton 6 held 100 ms; checkpoints at c5 (inside the continuous D3-D5 and D2-D5 runs) and c13, with lamp states asserted only where the other lamp has been unfed for at least one pad, because lamp cooling is a profile constant; maxMs 1000/2000 confine each until to the intended revolution across a wide run-rate range, and the relay terms identify the path. Not asserted: states during the D0 and D15 dwells (relay 4 coil, relay 3 coil and indicator lamp 3 in series from 4E while relay 5 holds D0; indicator lamps in coil paths); the pushbutton 5 stop and rest position, because 5X/6E puts relay 6 coil in series with the motor branch while the button is held, and a rest on D0 (relay 4 in, relay 5 out) or D15 (relays 4 and 5 in) back-feeds + to D16 and relay 6. The first-revolution JO depends on relay 4 latching during the starting D0 dwell; a failure at script[7] points there.
